summary: Forty-two minute manager 1-1. The first thirteen minutes are coffee talk and Chris holding Richard to a commitment to listen to a Sleep Token song in full, plus part of a second one. The remaining half is entirely mindset work rather than sales mechanics: Richard says his skill is fine but he has been badly in his own head since Saturday, and Chris coaches him on ego, fear, surrendering to the worst case, watching the mind, and a daily thirty-minute sit. Chris then checks whether Richard should take his calls at all that day, tries to reassign the 3pm and 5pm to Michael, and when that is not possible leaves the decision with Richard, who chooses to take them.
notable: No sales mechanics were coached. The entire session was consciousness work — ego, fear, surrender, meditation — which is consistent with the peer session earlier the same week where Michael prescribed journaling and the book Letting Go.

Richard describes acute performance anxiety in his own words: 'since Saturday... I just [have been] mindfucked the whole time' and 'there's so much fear and like things you don't know going on in here, which is coming out in the mouth, right. And just screwing up the calls. That's a hundred percent it.'

Richard confirms the Robert Karssiens call in this batch knocked him off: 'someone does come that does have money but he's like a hedge fund manager... he's like yeah well you're not gonna close me and it completely [messed] me up.'
He also confirms the Anthony Boon read — 'I had this very good call I think it was on Friday... it was so good but then the guy didn't have money.'

Chris offered to take him off live calls for the day and actively tried to reassign the 3pm and 5pm to Michael before leaving the choice with Richard: 'I want you to know there's no right or wrong with this.'

A third call is referenced that does not appear in this batch — a rebook where the prospect refused to turn his camera on and the rep continued anyway, describing it as 'such an awkward conversation'.

Richard is roughly a year out of a factory job building machines and had never closed before this year: 'a year ago, I was building machines... in a factory, and I'm living in a different country on my own.'
Richard references a previous $10,000 day and attributes it to a relaxed state rather than to technique.
Chris's framing of KPI attachment: 'You make it okay to not hit them... The attachment to hitting them is what also creates the suffering.'
In the opening small talk Chris jokes that very thin women would 'probably die' without high-calorie coffee drinks — an offhand remark from the sales manager of a fitness company.
